basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2-3.' and it opens '(Cap. XV.—Vers. 2, 3.) Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? Et ego vado sine liberis: et filius'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XV.—Vers. 2, 3.) Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? Et ego vado sine liberis: et filius Masec vernaculae meae, hic Damascus Eliezer. Et dixit Abram: Ecce mihi non dedisti semen: et filius vernaculae meae haeres meus erit. Ubi nos habemus, et filius Masec vernaculae meae: in Hebraeo scriptum est, UBEN MESECH BETHI: quod Aquila transtulit, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ποτίζοντος οἰκίαν μου: id est, filius potum dantis domui meae. Theodotio vero, καὶ υἱὸς τοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας μοῦ: id est, et filius ejus, qui super domum meam est. Quod autem dicit, hoc est: Ego sine liberis morior, et filius procuratoris mei, vel villici, qui universa dispensat et distribuit cibaria familiae meae, vocaturque Damascus Eliezer, hic meus haeres erit. Porro Eliezer interpretatur, Deus meus adjutor. Ab hoc aiunt Damascum et conditam, et nuncupatam.
